definition: A lens that is thicker in the middle than at the edges; it bends rays parallel to the principal axis so that they meet at the principal focus.
A lens that is thinner in the middle than at the edges; it spreads rays parallel to the principal axis apart so that they appear to come from the principal focus.
The distance from the centre of a lens to its principal focus.
The line that passes through the centre of a lens at right angles to the lens.

The point on the principal axis where rays parallel to the axis meet after passing through a converging lens, or appear to come from after passing through a diverging lens; also called the focal point.
An image formed where rays of light actually meet, so it can be formed on a screen; a real image made by a single converging lens is inverted.
A single converging lens held so that the object is closer to the lens than its principal focus, giving a virtual, upright, enlarged image.
An eye defect in which distant objects look sharp but near objects look blurred, because rays from a near object would focus behind the retina; it is corrected with a converging lens.
An eye defect in which near objects look sharp but distant objects look blurred, because rays from a distant object focus in front of the retina; it is corrected with a diverging lens.
